TriggerItems.Name: Make sure to copy this entire folder
- - - Modifier events - - -
TriggerItems.Description:
PreDamageEvent
==============
Issued before any armor is applied. This event uses the new 'DAMAGING' event.


ArmorDamageEvent
================
Issued after armor/mana shield type things are applied. This event uses the classic 'DAMAGED' event.

TriggerItems.Name: - - - Unique events - - -
TriggerItems.Description:
ZeroDamageEvent
===============
Occurs when a debuff is applied to a target unit. It's mainly useful in case someone wants to check if a unit has gained a specific debuff.

LethalDamageEvent
================
When a unit is about to die from the damage, this event intercepts that moment and allows the LethalDamageHP to be increased (if desired) to prevent death.

TriggerItems.Name: - - - Non-Modifier events - - -
TriggerItems.Description:
OnDamageEvent
===============
Does not allow the damage to be modified at this point. It's mainly used for cognitive distinction from the other events. Useful for analysis or for basic responses.

AfterDamageEvent
===============
Like OnDamageEvent, but occurs after the unit's HP has been changed.

TriggerItems.Name: - - - Wrap-up events - - -
TriggerItems.Description:
SourceDamageEvent
=================
Occurs when a source has completed dealing damage to a unit or to a group of units. The indicator for this distinction is an asynchronous (0 second) timer, or when an attack from a different unit is resolved.

AOEDamageEvent < DEPRECATED > Not recommended due to likelyhood of being useless.
===============
An early attempt to try to extract data from events that Blizzard didn't originally provide. It tracks when damage has hit multiple units in the same instant, but does not determine which one was the primary attacked unit. It also does not determine if splash damage hit only one unit.

TriggerItems.Name: - - - Deprecated - - -
TriggerItems.Description:
DamageModifierEvent & DamageEvent
===============================
These were the original events I created. I made a major API mistake when I introduced the PreDamageEvent by having it extend off of the existing DamageModifierEvent. DamageEvent was also split into the OnDamageEvent and ZeroDamageEvent, so these two events are now renamed to better suit their purposes.

DamageModifierEvent
=================
(real value < 4.00) is now is renamed to PreDamageEvent (with any real value)
(real value >= 4.00) is now renamed to ArmorDamageEvent (with any real value)

DamageEvent
===========
(real value == 2.00) is now renamed to ZeroDamageEvent
(real value == any other real value) is now renamed to OnDamageEvent

TriggerItems.Name: - - - Special Controls - - -
TriggerItems.Description:
RemoveDamageEvent
==================
(Very advanced) Run this trigger to un-register the current trigger from the system. Use at your own risk and only if you know what you're doing and why you're doing it.

DamageEventOverride
==================
Let's say you want to deal 'Pure' damage. Set this variable to 'true' from a PreDamageEvent, and you will prevent the execution of any higher-real-value events from being executed, as well as tell Damage Engine to ignore all normal WarCraft 3 modifications to that damage amount.

Parameters.Value: You can add extra classifications here if you want to differentiate between your triggered damage
Use DamageTypeExplosive (or any negative value damage type) if you want a unit killed by that damage to explode
The pre-defined type Code might be set by Damage Engine if Unit - Damage Target is detected and the user didn't define a type of their own.
"Pure" is especially important because it overrides both the Damage Engine as well as WarCraft 3 damage modification.
I therefore gave the user "Explosive Pure" in case one wants to combine the functionality of the two.
The following types are custom for the user only and do not have any significance to Damage Engine
other than telling it that the damage source is 'code' if setting NextDamageType to one of them
Inform the DamageEngine source code to initialize the debug strings.
This cannot be done during library/struct initialization because InitGlobals had not been called yet.
Due to weird GUI-vJass conflicts, I created Total Initialization for Lua.
UNLESS YOU KNOW WHAT YOU ARE DOING
A safety feature if infinite loops happened when Lock Instance is utilized, although theorically it should not be triggered at all
It is recommended to keep this at numbers ideally higher than generally possible instances until TSE is suspected of freezing the map due to loops

TriggerItems.Name: v1.7
TriggerItems.Description: - TSE__RemainingDuration can now be altered to modify the duration of the effect for OnIndex and OnLoop

TriggerItems.Name: v1.6
TriggerItems.Description:
- Fixed a bug that if the first effect created by TSE is a point effect, it will be affected by the new scale native and rendered it invisible
- Added a disabled theory trigger to showcase that Set Scale does not affect unit-attached effects
- Added an example of register event for both unit and point
- Added SourceUnitAliveCheck --> Solution for an issue discovered in v1.5
- Added OnEvent variables that allowed better readability of OnEvent triggers --> all are READ-ONLY
- MAJOR FIX: Resolve a hidden issue where indexes of TSE are not properly deallocated at times, especially after dealing with instances that has LockInstance = True
- Changed the timer scheme from using the add event to a Countdown Timer based approach due to 1.32+ patches having a limit of 100 Hz

TriggerItems.Name: v1.5
TriggerItems.Description: - Point is now preserved into the TSE data if declared and can be accessed via TSE_I_Point

TriggerItems.Name: v1.4
TriggerItems.Description:
- Added LockInstance capability
- Provided some Recursion safety for the Lock Instance feature, although it is more of additional safety layers

TriggerItems.Name: v1.3.1
TriggerItems.Description: - Fixed a critical bug with the newly added event feature

TriggerItems.Name: v1.3
TriggerItems.Description:
- Added ability to register triggers on events: OnIndexEvent, OnLoopEvent, OnEndEvent
> OnIndexEvent runs once the system finish indexing (register) all relevant data
> OnLoopEvent runs every TSE_TIMEOUT while the effect is active
> OnEndEvent runs when the system is about to deindex the instance

TriggerItems.Name: Unit Indexer
TriggerItems.Description:
This trigger works in two key phases:

1) During map initialization, enumerate all units of all players to give them an index.
2) Adds a second event to itself to index new units as they enter the map.

As a unit enters the map, check for any old units that may have been removed at some point in order to free their index.

Parameters.Value: This is the most important function - it provides an index for units as they enter the map
function IndexUnit takes nothing returns boolean
You can use the boolean UnitIndexerEnabled to protect some of your undesirable units from being indexed
-- Unit - Create 1 Dummy for (Triggering player) at TempLoc facing 0.00 degrees
You can also customize the following block - if conditions are false the (Matching unit) won't be indexed.
Generate a unique integer index for this unit
Link index to unit, unit to index
Use a doubly-linked list to store all active indexes
The next function is called each time a unit enters the map
function IndexNewUnit takes nothing returns boolean
Recycle indices of units no longer in-play every (15) units created
Recycle the index for later use
The next function initializes the core of the system
function InitializeUnitIndexer takes nothing returns nothing
This is the "Unit Indexer Initialized" event, use it instead of "Map Initialization" for best results
